question:
A 26-year-old pregnant woman, gravida 2, para 1, attends a prenatal care visit at 18 weeks of
gestation. She has a history of type 1 diabetes that was inadequately controlled prior to conception.
Her family history is unremarkable. Physical examination reveals a fundal height of 20 cm (7.9 in). An
abdominal ultrasound is performed. Which of the following congenital abnormalities is most likely to be
identified on the ultrasound? Answer Choices: (A) Neural tube defect (B) Hypoplastic left heart
syndrome (C) Coarctation of the aorta (D) Transposition of the great arteries (E) Anencephaly (F)
Tetralogy of Fallot (G) Ventricular septal defect (H) Sacral agenesis (I) Spina bifida (J) Atrial septal
defect
 A. Coarctation of the aorta
B. Spina bifida
C. Transposition of the great arteries
D. Sacral agenesis
E. Neural tube defect
F. Atrial septal defect
G. Tetralogy of Fallot
H. Hypoplastic left heart syndrome
I. Ventricular septal defect
J. Anencephaly
